papers.title: Beyond the Peak: Constraining early dark energy with the damping tail
papers.abstract: Early dark energy is commonly characterized by the amplitude and location of its primary energy-injection peak. We show that its post-peak evolution, which we call the \emph{EDE tail}, provides an additional observable probe of the underlying scalar dynamics and can materially affect its ability to alleviate the Hubble tension. We construct a simple phenomenological framework in which distinct regions of a multiscale scalar potential govern the dynamics at different field scales. As a representative realization, we consider a potential that combines axion-like and $\alpha$-attractor-like regimes, thereby allowing the EDE tail to be reshaped through reflection and asymmetric oscillations. Confronting this framework with cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and supernova observations, we find an improved fit to the high-$\ell$ CMB data together with a higher inferred bestfit $H_0$. Our results show that the EDE tail retains observable information about the underlying scalar potential that is not captured by the conventional peak parameters alone. This provides a complementary route for constructing and observationally distinguishing EDE scenarios, and potentially for further alleviating the Hubble tension.

papers.title: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
papers.abstract: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar curvature region, which prevents the Universe from evolving into the anti-gravity or having a ghost graviton region, without the fine-tuning of the initial conditions. We also discuss how this regime can be tested using peculiar velocity and kSZ effect probes.

papers.title: Features investigated: A detailed study of axion monodromy inflation using CLiENT
papers.abstract: We investigate features in the primordial power spectrum from inflation, specifically those predicted by the axion monodromy model, using recent observational data. In order to compute posteriors, profile likelihoods and Bayesian evidence accurately for the complex likelihood surfaces arising in this model we have used the CLiENT emulator framework. As our data combinations we use both a "conservative" set consisting of Planck PR4 temperature, polarisation and lensing data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more "aggressive" set which also includes small-scale CMB data from ACT and SPT. We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data. With the conservative data the best fit lies at a frequency $\omega \simeq 51$ and lowers $\chi^2$ by 10.1 relative to a featureless spectrum. However, this feature is disfavoured by the more aggressive data combination, whose best fit lies at $\omega \simeq 31$ and lowers $\chi^2$ by 7.4. Fits to featureless data are known to give similar improvements, and the Akaike information criterion, the Bayes factors and the look-elsewhere effect all indicate that neither improvement is significant. The amplitude is limited to $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.056$ and $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.062$ (95%) for the two datasets. The emulators reproduce the true log-likelihood at samples of their posteriors with rms errors of 0.07 and 0.16, and the profile likelihoods are calculated with the true likelihood, using the profile capability of CLiENT.

papers.title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
papers.abstract: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $\lambda$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|\lambda|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|\lambda|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|\lambda|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|\lambda|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

papers.title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $\eta$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
papers.abstract: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.

papers.title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
papers.abstract: We investigate how matter fields affect spacetime regularity in a class of gravitational theories with second-order field equations in spherical symmetry, of which general relativity is a special case, and which may encode effective corrections from an underlying quantum theory of gravity. Focusing on spherically symmetric black holes and cosmological spacetimes in theories in which vacuum spacetimes display bounded curvature invariants, we derive the conditions under which regular geometries can be supported by static and perturbative scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids. We discuss the impact of matter on the regularity requirements of curvature boundedness and geodesic completeness relative to vacuum, finding in general that coupling to matter does not eliminate the existence of theories with regular solutions.

papers.title: Quantum computing for gearing down complex many-fermion problems
papers.abstract: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scale {\it ab initio} calculations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain challenging. We introduce a quantum-classical framework that identifies compact single-particle bases to bring otherwise intractable many-fermion problems within classical reach while preserving an accurate ground-state description. We develop an efficient adaptive search scheme driven by simulated annealing that jointly optimizes natural-orbital-guided transformations and active-space selections. A quantum-assisted ground-state estimator provides search guidance using low-depth circuits and relaxed accuracy requirements, making the framework promising for NISQ devices. We demonstrate the framework's applicability for the nuclear structure of the oxygen isotopes. Our framework opens a new route to tackling complex {\it ab initio} many-fermion problems across disciplines through quantum-assisted basis reduction.

papers.title: Chromatic calorimetry using nanocomposites: status and future challenges
papers.abstract: The development of advanced detector technologies will play a key role in future high-energy physics experiments, such as the FCC-ee. In this context, chromatic calorimetry is an emerging concept for electromagnetic calorimeters, with the potential to combine the precise energy measurement of homogeneous calorimeters with longitudinal reconstruction of particle showers. The state of the art in chromatic calorimetry is reviewed, including experimental results from proof-of-concept prototypes and simulation studies investigating quantum-dot-based configurations. Recent progress and current challenges in the development of nanocomposites are also discussed. Finally, future prospects for chromatic calorimetry are outlined.

papers.title: Disk 2-point functions for conformal loop ensemble: a derivation from the SLE loop CFT
papers.abstract: We give a derivation of the bulk two-point functions of two-dimensional critical loop models in the disk based on conformal loop ensembles (CLE) and the conformal field theory of SLE loop measures developed by Baverez--Jego. Combining local Ward identities with the spectral resolution of the SLE-loop CFT, we express the two-point functions as contour integrals involving known CLE three-point structure constants and Virasoro conformal blocks. With a suitable choice of contour, these integrals are absolutely convergent and provide a unified representation of a broad class of correlation functions, valid for both irrational and rational central charges. For irrational central charges, evaluating these integrals by residues determines the discrete closed-channel spectrum and yields expansions that agree with the analytic bootstrap predictions of Downing--Jacobsen--Nivesvivat--Ribault--Saleur.

papers.title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
papers.abstract: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gau{\ss}ian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand. In combination, we reduce the sampling task for a general class of complex systems to a Gau{\ss}ian one, and the main computational task is that of computing the PIK. We illustrate the approach with the one-site Hubbard model at arbitrary chemical potential and with $\phi^4$-deformed extensions of it.

papers.title: Quantum Many-Body Scars from Operator Size
papers.abstract: We present a general construction of approximate many-body scar states in two copies of a system using a bilocal size interaction that couples one site to its partner on the other copy. For an uncoupled two-sided Hamiltonian whose terms have fixed size in an operator basis, we identify polynomially many Krylov basis states that it annihilates and that, in the thermodynamic limit, become concentrated on a single size sector. The size operator splits them into a tower of equally spaced levels that gives rise to coherent revivals characterized by collective oscillations of energy across the two copies. We provide a concrete realization of this construction in two copies of a general $q$-body nearest-neighbor spin chain, and the SYK model.
